newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat broadly steady as EU harvests start.
newsitem.headline: German wheat broadly steady as EU harvests start.

text.p: German wheat prices are holding steady in slow trade as buyers and sellers await harvest reports from other European countries, especially France, traders said on Wednesday.
Germany's wheat harvest is still four weeks off, but barley is being cut in the southwest and the southeast.
"Small new crop wheat volumes have traded at slight discounts but new activity depends on what happens in France," one broker said.
"Volumes and yield there look good, but sellers here hope that quality may have suffered, which would open more opportunities for German wheat."
Flooding in the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland, which had damaged crops and might raise import demand later this year, was neutral on prices in Germany.
Traders said eastern German states might be able to supply wheat to those countries once import requirements had been clarified.
Getting supplies and services back on track appeared to be the priority in the affected regions.
German grain sellers would also face competition from Hungary.
Traders were looking to the EU export tender on Thursday to give direction on wheat as well as authorising barley rebates to facilitate German exports to Saudi Arabia.
Sellers feard the EU would award only small rebates, under the impression that large world wheat crops were in the pipeline. That would weigh on prices.
Wheat prices were underpinned by the absence of feed wheat offers from Britain, where the currency is prohibitively high versus the mark.
Nominal German fob levels for new crop wheat were unchanged at 270-300 marks a tonne, basis first half September and 3,000 tonne lots.
Fob Rostock/Hamburg wheat with 14 percent protein was quoted at 310 marks basis 20,000 tonnes.
Ex-crop barley was at around 235 fob and rye at 242.50-247.50, both unchanged.
Old crop wheat supplies were dwindling -- 14 percent spot wheat was sold out, with other grades at 270-280 marks fob.
